more.title: Exquisite X-rays and dynamic compression initiate a new era of physics experiments on plutonium
more.summary: Scientists at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), Argonne National Laboratory (ANL) and Washington State University (WSU) have conducted the first dynamic compression experiments on plutonium at a national light source facility, the Dynamic Compression Sector (DCS).

more.title: New discovery reveals what may be holding back room-temperature superconductors
more.summary: A major breakthrough in superconductivity research has revealed that one of the essential ingredients for electricity to flow without resistance can exist at room temperature. Scientists discovered that electrons can form stable pairs at much higher temperatures than previously understood, suggesting that a different obstacle may be preventing room-temperature superconductivity.

more.title: MIT discovers that aging weakens the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
more.summary: MIT researchers have discovered that the brain’s natural waste-removal system becomes significantly less effective during sleep as people age. The decline is linked to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and changes in blood flow, potentially offering new clues about why aging increases the risk of Alzheimer's disease and dementia.

more.title: Ancient minerals reveal a missing chapter in Türkiye's mountain-building history
more.summary: A mountain range can bear the marks of events from tens of millions of years ago. The challenge lies in determining when each mark was created. In southern Türkiye's Central Taurides, scientists have developed a method to date some of these ancient movements by examining tiny calcite deposits that formed as faults shifted. This new timeline alters the region's geological history.

more.title: New mixing benchmark could help industry reduce energy use in stirred tanks
more.summary: Solid–liquid mixing, where particles are dispersed in a liquid, is essential in many industrial processes such as slurry preparation, crystallization, precipitation, adsorption and dissolution. In such cases, effective mixing is critical for contact between particles and liquid, enabling mass transfer.

more.title: Researchers trace how gut microbes transform dietary plant sterols into circulating sulfated metabolites
more.summary: Phytosterols are plant-derived compounds found in vegetable oils, nuts and seeds. They are studied for their ability to reduce cholesterol absorption, yet only about 5% enter the circulation and most are excreted. How gut bacteria influence their metabolism and tissue distribution has remained unclear.

more.title: Should we save every old building?
more.summary: When you visit one of Norway's open-air museums, you can experience a piece of old Norway: log-built timber houses, farmsteads and farm complexes, often situated in a historic cultural landscape.

more.title: Watch: Sea level rise isn't just waves—how groundwater threatens coastal cities from below
more.summary: With El Niño winter storms rolling in, coastal communities will naturally brace for the obvious: surging high tides, pounding waves and seawater spilling over seawalls. Decades of storm coverage have encouraged us to measure climate risk by what crashes onto the shoreline.

more.title: First lunar-specific ground motion model could guide seismic hazard assessments on moon
more.summary: Civil engineers looking forward to building structures on the moon need to know how ground motion from moonquakes will affect these buildings. But will ground motion models developed for Earth work well for the lunar landscape?

more.title: More than a billion years of Earth's history vanished. Scientists may finally know why
more.summary: Scientists may have finally explained why up to more than a billion years of Earth's geological history are missing from rocks around the world. New research suggests that powerful currents deep inside the planet slowly raised and lowered entire continents, allowing erosion to erase vast stretches of geological history before they were buried and preserved.
